newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine traders see big wheat sales to Brazil.
newsitem.headline: Argentine traders see big wheat sales to Brazil.

text.p: Argentine traders scoffed Wednesday at reports Canada sold 600,000 tonnes of wheat to Brazil and said their traditional customer will soon be sniffing around for two million tonnes more of their grain.
"Brazil isn't covered in March, April or May despite the 600,000 tonnes that I sincerely believe are just a rumor for the moment," one trader told Reuters.
"If the Canada deal was done, it was done for July or later," he said.
Canadian trade sources said earlier this week that the Canadian Wheat Board (CWB) sold up to 600,000 tonnes of milling wheat at $150 a tonne for May/July delivery.
The CWB would not confirm the deal, but a spokesman suggested that the reported price was too low. Brazilian traders said that they had just heard rumors of the deal.
"This does not exist, it is a lie!" another trader said, "These are rumors put about to drive down the price of Argentine wheat."
He added that if the deal had really happened the Brazilian buyers would have provided documentary evidence to add to their bargaining clout with the Argentines.
The first trader said $150 sounded too expensive.
"So, $150 FOB, plus the $15 tax for imports from outside (the Mercosur trade bloc), that makes $165," he said, "I don't think they would pay a premium of $7 for Canadian wheat over Argentine."
He said export quality Argentine wheat was offered at $165 FOB for Brazil, but that transport to Brazil was $7 a tonne cheaper than for the Canadians.
But Brazilian millers say they might have to import Canadian wheat to mix with Argentine grain, whose quality they said was below par this season.
A market source said Tuesday Argentine exporters had sold a total of between 8.0 million and 8.3 million tonnes of 1996/97 wheat, out of likely total sales of about 11 million tonnes.
But Brazil was lagging behind, only having bought about two million tonnes, compared to purchases of three million tonnes of Argentine wheat at the same point last season.
The traders said they expected the Brazilians would soon make up for lost ground.
"Of the 2.6 million tonnes of Argentine wheat still to sell, I think Brazil will take two million tonnes," one said.
But he admitted that the Brazilians were just making small purchases at the moment.
"They are buying small quantities every day, just about 7,000 or 8,000 tonnes, to cover spot needs," he said.
